note: Delivery presets for --for. Safe zones are conservative fractions of the frame covered by each app's own UI (buttons, captions, progress bars); apps change their UI, so keep important text well inside them and check the preview. Size limits are the smallest common limit (free tiers).

tiktok.label: TikTok
tiktok.cover: Pick a cover frame in the app; use the poster's moment.
tiktok.notes: Right rail holds like/comment/share; bottom holds the caption and sound name. Plays muted-to-sound, loops.

reels.label: Instagram Reels
reels.cover: Upload shipreel.jpg cropped to 1080x1920; the grid shows the center 1080x1350.
reels.notes: Grid crops to 4:5, so keep the hook inside the center 1080x1350. Autoplays muted in feed.

shorts.label: YouTube Shorts
shorts.cover: Chosen from the video frames in YouTube Studio.
shorts.notes: Channel name, title, and subscribe button sit over the bottom; actions on the right.

x.label: X
x.cover: X uses frame 0 — the baked poster.
x.notes: Autoplays muted in the timeline. Put the link in a reply for reach.

linkedin.label: LinkedIn
linkedin.cover: Upload shipreel.jpg as the thumbnail in the post editor.
linkedin.notes: 4:5 takes the most feed height on mobile. Autoplays muted; also accepts an .srt upload.

youtube.label: YouTube
youtube.cover: Upload a 1280x720 thumbnail made from shipreel.jpg.
youtube.notes: Upload shipreel.srt as subtitles; the progress bar covers the bottom edge on hover.

producthunt.label: Product Hunt
producthunt.cover: Gallery images are 1270x760; export stills from the review frames.
producthunt.notes: The gallery video is a YouTube link — upload the YouTube export first.

readme.label: GitHub README
readme.cover: The GIF's first frame; frame 0 is the baked poster.
readme.notes: Drag the MP4 into the README editor to host it (10 MB on free plans). MP4s do not autoplay there; the GIF does.

discord.label: Discord
discord.cover: Discord shows frame 0 — the baked poster.
discord.notes: Free uploads are capped at 10 MB, so the export is re-encoded to fit.

instagram-feed.label: Instagram feed
instagram-feed.cover: Upload a custom cover; the profile grid crops it to 1080x1350.
instagram-feed.notes: Feed videos are served as Reels. The caption and audio strip sit under the frame; keep the last line clear of the bottom.

stories.label: Instagram Stories
stories.cover: No cover; the first frame is what people see.
stories.notes: Each card is 15s, so use --stories to split. Profile row and close friends label sit at the top; the reply bar covers the bottom.

facebook.label: Facebook feed
facebook.cover: Choose a thumbnail at upload; use shipreel.jpg.
facebook.notes: 4:5 is the tallest the feed shows without cropping. Autoplays muted.

facebook-reels.label: Facebook Reels
facebook-reels.cover: Pick a cover frame in the composer.
facebook-reels.notes: Same furniture as Instagram Reels: right rail of buttons, caption across the bottom.

threads.label: Threads
threads.notes: Up to 5 minutes. Autoplays muted in the feed; vertical and square both display well.

bluesky.label: Bluesky
bluesky.notes: Up to 10 minutes and 300 MB; playback is capped around 720p, so keep text large. Add alt text on the post.

mastodon.label: Mastodon
mastodon.notes: Limits are set per instance; 40 MB is the common default (mastodon.social allows more). Check your instance and add a media description.

reddit.label: Reddit
reddit.notes: Direct uploads go up to 1 GB, 15 minutes, 1080p30. Autoplays muted in feeds, so burn the captions.

snapchat.label: Snapchat Spotlight
snapchat.cover: Pick a cover in the app.
snapchat.notes: 5–60s, sound required, no watermarks from other apps. 15–30s performs best.

pinterest.label: Pinterest
pinterest.cover: Upload a cover image; Pinterest shows it before play.
pinterest.notes: 2:3 (1000x1500) is the native pin shape; 9:16 also works. 6–15s performs best.

whatsapp.label: WhatsApp status
whatsapp.cover: No cover; the first frame is what people see.
whatsapp.notes: 16 MB and 30s per clip — the tightest budget here, so the export is re-encoded to fit.

telegram.label: Telegram
telegram.notes: 2 GB per file. Channels autoplay muted; square and vertical also display well.

slack.label: Slack
slack.notes: 1 GB per file, but workspaces have a shared storage cap, so a 1280-wide export is the polite size. Plays inline, muted until clicked.

vimeo.label: Vimeo
vimeo.notes: Free accounts have a weekly upload quota rather than a per-file cap. Upload shipreel.srt as a caption track.

devto.label: dev.to
devto.notes: Posts are markdown: embed the GIF, or a YouTube/Vimeo link with {% embed %}. Images upload up to 25 MB.

appstore.label: App Store preview
appstore.cover: App Store Connect picks a poster frame; choose the strongest.
appstore.notes: Apple requires exactly 886x1920 for iPhone previews, so the vertical render is centre-cropped — 97px comes off each side, which is why this preset reserves wider margins. 15-30s, H.264 + AAC, and it must show real app footage: use --capture or --footage.

googleplay.label: Google Play preview
googleplay.notes: Play takes a YouTube URL, not an upload: publish the landscape render on YouTube (public, not age-restricted, not monetised) and paste the plain video URL. Only the first 30s autoplays.
